page: Amazon Web Services i4i.16xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage is a key feature, consisting of 15,000 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by a 38 Gbps baseline bandwidth. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and specialized execution capabilities. The server achieves a strong multi-core CPU performance score of 61,946.14 in stress-ng and a PassMark CPU score of 57,600.73. Database operations are highly efficient, scoring in the top 25% on PassMark database tests with 26,317.04 operations. Static web serving throughput is also strong at 45.18 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is average, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,688.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1,893.69. Memory bandwidth tests, such as large-block uncached reads at 165.49 GB/sec, fall into the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i4i.16xlarge offers a high density of local NVMe storage coupled with a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, making it a resource-dense option for data-intensive deployments without the overhead of external storage attachments. The hardware profile is suited for large-scale database systems, software compilation, static web serving, and moderate language model inference tasks, though it is constrained by average single-threaded execution speeds.
